claims.summary: Eles and elas are third-person plural personal pronouns in Portuguese, with different usage based on gender and formality.
As subjects, 'eles' and 'elas' are used with the same verb form, differing only in gender agreement.
When used after prepositions, 'eles' and 'elas' maintain their forms, such as 'com eles', 'para elas', and 'deles'/'delas'.
In colloquial Brazilian Portuguese, 'eles/elas' can also function as direct objects, such as 'Eu vi eles ontem'.

The choice of 'eles' or 'elas' depends on the grammatical gender of the nouns they replace, and their usage as direct objects is more common in spoken Brazilian Portuguese than in formal written Portuguese.
